_note: The forum event list (PRD E22-S2; docs/data-sources.md 2.4, build step 19): public conference and association event pages (speaker lists, programs, agendas) that the briefer reads for bank.memberships when it researches a bank. src/events.mjs picks the events for the bank's metros, then its states, then national ones, at most maxPerAccount, and passes them to the briefer as fenced data. A rule file: events only, NO person's name and NO prospect data. PUBLIC PAGES ONLY: never an attendee list, a members-only directory or a page behind a login. A URL whose path, query or subdomain suggests one (attendee, member, login, portal, a member directory) is refused on load, as are plain http, credentials, ports and tracking parameters. FIELDS: id (lowercase, hyphens); name; host (who runs the event); url (the public speaker, program or agenda page); dates {start, end} as YYYY-MM-DD; association (as a principal writes it for a membership in the firm's network, src/network.mjs, so a forum route can match it); national (true: every bank) or states (two-letter codes) and metros (CBSA codes from metros.json); termsCheckedOn (the day a principal read the site's terms of use, YYYY-MM-DD). An entry with no termsCheckedOn, or with [CONFIRM] anywhere in it (its note included), is a PLACEHOLDER: checked on load, never passed to the briefer. EVERY ENTRY BELOW IS A PLACEHOLDER: nothing was fetched from the environment that wrote this file, so each URL, date and scope comes from the research in docs/listening-sources.md B.5 and is unconfirmed. To use an entry, a principal opens the page, checks that it is public, reads the site's terms, fills in the URL and the dates, sets termsCheckedOn to that day, and removes [CONFIRM] from its note. Then run npm test (it checks this file) and outbound research run --account ID --dry-run to see the pages an account gets. Every value here, maxPerAccount included, is a PLACEHOLDER for a principal to review.
